claim: Self-consistency across sampled responses is a more reliable measure of model confidence than log-probability-based scores, and this paper builds an abstention method by having the LLM self-evaluate similarity between its own sampled responses.
stance_target: the target paper's core premise: repeated-sampling confidence outperforms expressed/log-probability confidence
quoted_support: Building on earlier approaches that use self-consistency as a more reliable measure of model confidence, we propose using the LLM itself to self-evaluate the similarity between each of its sampled responses for a given query.

claim: Conformal prediction techniques applied to a self-consistency-based confidence signal yield an abstention procedure with rigorous theoretical guarantees on the hallucination (error) rate.
stance_target: feasibility of a formally-guaranteed downstream action built directly on a sampling-based confidence signal
scope_conditions: general-domain QA, requires conformal calibration set
quoted_support: We then further leverage conformal prediction techniques to develop an abstention procedure that benefits from rigorous theoretical guarantees on the hallucination rate (error rate).

claim: The conformal abstention method reliably bounds hallucination rate on multiple open-domain QA datasets while maintaining a significantly LESS conservative (higher-coverage) abstention rate than log-probability-based baselines on long-response data (Temporal Sequences), and comparable performance on short-answer data (TriviaQA).
stance_target: self-consistency/sampling-based confidence, when turned into an abstention policy, beats log-probability confidence on the accuracy-coverage tradeoff, at least for long-form responses
scope_conditions: Temporal Sequences (long responses) and TriviaQA (short answers) datasets
quoted_support: our resulting conformal abstention method reliably bounds the hallucination rate on various closed-book, open-domain generative question answering datasets, while also maintaining a significantly less conservative abstention rate on a dataset with long responses (Temporal Sequences) compared to baselines using log-probability scores to quantify uncertainty, while achieveing comparable performance on a dataset with short answers (TriviaQA).

claim: This general-domain conformal abstention method uses LLM-judged similarity to determine response equivalence, whereas a code-generation analogue could substitute an execution-based equivalence check (as in Task Abstention, 2605.17029), which would remove reliance on a second LLM-as-judge call and its own calibration uncertainty.
stance_target: methodological template transferable to code with a cleaner ground-truth equivalence check (execution outcomes) than general QA affords
scope_conditions: cross-paper comparison; not stated directly in this abstract
quoted_support: we use a thresholded similarity function to determine if two responses match, but also provide a method for calibrating the threshold based on conformal prediction
